 Judgment
This petition is filed by the minor petitioner through his guardian/natural father U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road Traffic Accident. 
2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that, on 01.10.2022 at about 2.30 p.m., he was proceeding as a pillion rider on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-53-HL-3490 ridden SCCH 11 3 MVC.No.5774/2022 by his father Sri.Suresha.D.V., when he stopped his vehicle infront of SLV Bakery and waiting for a traffic signal, at that time one Crane bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MB-5900 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor cycle. Due to which, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent .4,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant and other incidental charges. 
Prior to the accidental injuries, he was hale and healthy and was a student. Due to the accidental injuries he become permanent disabled. The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of crane by its driver. The respondents being the owner and insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. 
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal, hence he has been placed as SCCH 11 4 MVC.No.5774/2022 ex-parte. The respondent No.2 appeared before tribunal through his counsel and filed his written statement. 
4. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement. In the written statement it is stated that, the petition is not maintainable in law and facts and hence liable to be dismissed. Further this respondent has denied the age, occupation, income of petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner,
injuries sustained by the petitioner and also the amount spent towards medical treatment. Further this respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy vide No.73080131220100000826 valid from 14.07.2022 to 13.07.2023 in respect of a Crane bearing No.KA-51-MB-5900 in favour of 1st respondent and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy. Further contended that due to own negligence of minor petitioner's father being the rider of motor cycle without taking proper precaution for safety of minor pillion rider with an intention to jump traffic signal unable to succeed his attempt came to sudden halt and SCCH 11 5 MVC.No.5774/2022 minor petitioner who was not intact on pillion seat, fell down due to negligence of rider of motor cycle. 
Further there was no accident caused by insured crane. Further contended that the rider of motor cycle had no valid driving license authorizing him to ride the motor cycle. Further the rider and Rohith Gowda Alias Rohith .S vs Manivannan Sivan on 6 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114466887/
2 pillion rider were not wearing safety helmet. Further contended that the driver of crane had no valid and effective driving license at the time of alleged accident. The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant. Among other grounds prays for dismissal of the petition. 
5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 01.10.2022 at about 2.30 p.m., infront of SLV Bakery, Ibbaluru Junction,
Bengaluru, when he was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-53- HL-3490 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Crane bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MB-5900 by its driver? 
SCCH 11 6 MVC.No.5774/2022 2. Whether petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award? 
6. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the natural guardian/father of minor petitioner has been examined as PW.1 and Dr.R.Shashikanth, who was working as Medical Officer at Manipal Hospital has been examined as PW.2 and got marked 12 documents at Ex.P.1 to 20 and closed his side of evidence. The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary. 
7. I have heard arguments on both side and perused the materials available on record. 
8. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative. 
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
 SCCH 11 7 MVC.No.5774/2022  //REASONS//
 9. Issue No.1:- The guardian of minor petitioner Rohith Gowda Alias Rohith .S vs Manivannan Sivan on 6 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114466887/
3 contended that on 01.10.2022 at about 2.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-53-HL-3490 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Crane bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MB-5900 by its driver he sustained grievous injuries. 
10. In order to prove negligence driving of Crane bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MB-5900 by its driver, the guardian of minor petitioner i.e., father has examined himself as PW.1 and deposed that due to negligent driving of crane by its driver the accident occurred. The respondents nothing elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner. 
11. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 and 2, FIR and first information. On perusal of Ex.P.1 and 2, FIR and first information, one Sri.Suresh.D.V., S/o.Venkateshappa, has lodged complaint with the police on SCCH 11 8 MVC.No.5774/2022 02.10.2022 and accident occurred on 01.10.2022. After registration the case, the police went near the place of accident and drew up spot mahazar & sketch marked at Ex.P.11 & 12 by narrating the place of accident. As per Ex.P.3 - IMV Report, damages to vehicle. Ex.P4 is the wound certificate, on perusal of the same reveals that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are simple as well as grievous in nature. After completion of the investigation, the police have filed Ex.P5 - charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
12. On meticulous perusal of entire record, it clearly shows that only due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle the accident occurred. The respondents nothing placed before the tribunal to prove negligence of petitioner. So, the materials placed by the petitioner clearly show that the accident occurred due to negligence of driving of Crane bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MB-5900 by its driver and SCCH 11 9 MVC.No.5774/2022 petitioner sustained injuries. Accordingly, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative. 
13. Issue No.2: In view of held issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation. To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance. 
14. The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained grievous injuries and said injuries are grievous in nature. In order to prove the injuries sustained by him, the guardian of petitioner has produced wound certificate and discharge summaries which are marked at Ex.P4 and 7. On perusal of Ex.P.4 & 7 it reveals that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries. On perusal of Ex.P.7 - Discharge summary issued by Manipal Hospitals, wherein doctor diagnosed that petitioner has sustained displaced fracture of both bones of SCCH 11 10 MVC.No.5774/2022 right forearm middle 3rd - type 1 open fracture and underwent manipulation under GA + Debridement + TENS nailing for right both bone forearm fracture under GA on 02.10.2022 and he took treatment as an inpatient Rohith Gowda Alias Rohith .S vs Manivannan Sivan on 6 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114466887/
4 from 01.10.2022 to 04.10.2022 and again from 21.10.2023 & 22.10.2023 i.e., for a period of 06 days.
15 . PW2/Doctor deposed in his evidence that petitioner has sustained displaced fracture of both bones (radius & ulna) of right forearm, punctured wound present over distal aspect of right forearm 0.2cm x 2cms x bone deep and abrasion present over dorso lateral aspect of right forearm and doctor has opined that injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 & 3 are simple in nature and underwent surgery of under general anesthesia for right forearm fracture manipulation fractured reduction and internal fixation and debridement with tens nailing of right radius and ulna was done on 02.10.2022 and later discharged. PW.2 doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability. Further, the doctor also produced SCCH 11 11 MVC.No.5774/2022 MLC, police intimation, disability assessment with calculation sheet, X-ray films and two case sheets marked at Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.20. The doctor has assessed the disability of 37.64% to the right upper limb and 12.54% to the whole body. 
16. In the petition the age of the petitioner by name Master Rohith Gowda is shown as 13 years. In order to prove the age of minor petitioner, the father of minor petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 25.08.2009 and accident occurred on 01.10.2022, so the age of petitioner was 13 years as on the date of accident. As per the petition and Wound certificate, the age of petitioner shown as 13 years. In Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Ltd and another, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:
If the disability is upto 10% to the whole body .1 lakh, above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, .3 lakhs: upto 60%, .4 lakhs, Upto 90% .5 lakhs and above 90% it should be .6 lakhs. 
SCCH 11 12 MVC.No.5774/2022 For all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc. Case on hand the doctor gave disability 12.54% to the whole body. But by considering the injuries, occupation and facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal considered that there is 10% functional disability. As per Master Mallikarjun case, the disability upto 10% to the whole body - .1 lakh. Accordingly the petitioner is entitled for .1,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.
17. Towards Medical Expenses: 
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses. The petitioner contended that he has spent more than .4,00,000/- towards his medical,
conveyance and transportation charges. The petitioner has produced 07 medical bills at Ex.P.9 for .1,86,176/- and 3 medical bills SCCH 11 13 MVC.No.5774/2022 marked at Ex.P.14 for .62,803/- + .655/- + .500/- = .63,958/-. In Ex.P.14 - Final bill Rohith Gowda Alias Rohith .S vs Manivannan Sivan on 6 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114466887/
5 .62,803/-, out of that .44,352/- paid by Medi Assist India Private Limited Share and remaining amount of .18,214/- paid by petitioner. Hence the petitioner is entitled for .2,05,545/- under the head medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization. 
18. Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner has contended that his son was student and he has hospitalized due to injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident. So, when the father/mother of the petitioner was in the hospital along with petitioner, he has no income during that period. As such the petitioner is entitled for lump sum of .20,000/- under the head Discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization. 
19. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
SCCH 11 14 MVC.No.5774/2022 Sl.No. Particulars Amount.
a. Pain and suffering already .1,00,000/-
undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability. 
b. Towards medical and .2,05,545/-
incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization. 
c. Discomfort, inconvenience .20,000/-
and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization Total Compensation .3,25,545/-
The petitioner is also entitled for compensation of .3,25,545/-.
20. In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to SCCH 11 15 MVC.No.5774/2022 the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law. Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Rohith Gowda Alias Rohith .S vs Manivannan Sivan on 6 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114466887/
6 Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908. Thus,
in the given circumstances of this case, interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded." 
In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. 
21. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2. It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Crane bearing Regn.No.KA-51-MB-5900 by its driver. The police have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act. So, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the SCCH 11 16 MVC.No.5774/2022 petitioner. Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative. 
22. Issue No.3: .For the forgoing reasons and in view of the above discussion I proceed to pass the following: 
ORDER The claim petition filed by the guardian of minor petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost. 
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .3,25,545/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Twenty Five Thousand Five Hundred and Forty Five only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization. 
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner. Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award. 
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 60% shall be released in the name of guardian of minor petitioner and the SCCH 11 17 MVC.No.5774/2022 remaining 40% kept in FD in the name of minor petitioner in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till he attain the age of majority whichever is later. The guardian of petitioner is entitled to receive interest that accrues on FD periodically. 
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019. 
The guardian of minor petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of guardian of minor petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank. Further guardian of minor Rohith Gowda Alias Rohith .S vs Manivannan Sivan on 6 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114466887/
7 petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhaar Card. 
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent Insurance Company, the guardian of minor petitioner is SCCH 11 18 MVC.No.5774/2022 entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal. 
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal. 
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to her account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court. 
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1000/-. Draw award accordingly.
